name: select
title: Select
description: Select. Best for: One choice from a list of about five options or more.

files.content: import { Fragment, type AriaAttributes, type ComponentPropsWithoutRef, type ReactNode, type Ref } from 'react' import { Select as RadixSelect } from 'radix-ui' import { Check, ChevronDown } from 'lucide-react' import { cn } from '../../../lib/cn' import { disabledText } from '../../../lib/disabled' import { inputVariants } from '../input/Input' export type SelectOption = { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean } /** A Select row: a `SelectOption` plus an optional leading icon. Kept as its own type rather than * an `icon` field on `SelectOption`, because MultiSelect takes `SelectOption[]` too and renders * no icons: widening the shared type would let an icon compile there and vanish. */ export type SelectOptionWithIcon = SelectOption & { /** Leading glyph, aria-hidden: the label names the row. Not repeated in the trigger. */ icon?: ReactNode } /** A titled run of rows. The heading is not selectable; it names the group for screen readers. */ export type SelectGroup = { label: string; options: SelectOptionWithIcon[] } /** The list comes in one of two shapes, never both: flat `options`, or `groups` with headings. */ type SelectList = | { options: SelectOptionWithIcon[]; groups?: never } | { groups: SelectGroup[]; options?: never } /** `RadixSelect.Root`'s own prop type (`SelectSharedProps & { value, defaultValue, * onValueChange }`, read from `@radix-ui/react-select`'s `.d.mts`) has no index signature and no * `aria-*`/`data-*`/`className`. Passing anything outside that closed set as a *top-level* prop * to `` compiled cleanly, `data-testid` was destructured into `rest`, * spread onto `RadixSelect.Root` (a context provider with no DOM node of its own), and never * reached any element in the render tree — silently, with no type error and no runtime error. * That is worse than a same-element override (Input/Textarea/Checkbox/Radio's shape): there, a * caller-supplied prop at least *lands somewhere*, just not where it's supposed to win; here it * landed nowhere at all. Same root cause as `IconButton`'s original `aria-label` `Omit` * and Avatar's — the hyphenated-key exemption — but a new failure mode: silent disappearance, * not silent override. * * Fix: a second, explicit rest path — `triggerProps` — typed against * `RadixSelect.Trigger`'s own props and spread onto that element, which is the actual visible, * interactive DOM node. `SelectTriggerRestProps` excludes `'aria-label'`, `'aria-invalid'`, * `'id'` and `'aria-describedby'` by redeclaring each `never` rather than `Omit`-ing them alone. * `aria-describedby` needs the redeclaration because `Omit` alone is inert against a hyphenated * key. `id` is an ordinary key, so a caller passing a literal `triggerProps={{ id: 'x' }}` is * already rejected by `Omit` alone, through ordinary excess-property checking — but that checking * only fires on a fresh literal, and this file's own tests prove a guard load-bearing with a * non-literal value instead (assigned to a `const` first, which bypasses excess-property checking * regardless of the key's shape — see the comment on the `aria-label`/`aria-invalid` tests in * `Select.test.tsx`). Against that shape the `Omit` entry for `id` does nothing; `id?: never` is * what actually rejects it, and is the one doing real work here. Do not delete it on the reasoning * that `Omit` already covers `id` — it only covers the literal case nothing here tests for. The * `id`/`aria-describedby` tests also give their non-literal object a second, genuinely valid prop * (`onClick`) alongside the banned key. That is not a guard against TypeScript's "no properties in * common" weak-type check (TS2559) — `SelectTriggerRestProps`'s own `` [key: `data-${string}`]: * unknown `` index signature (below) already makes the type non-weak, so TS2559 never runs against * it today. The extra prop is insurance against that index signature being removed later: without * it, a single-key object would put TS2559 back in play and a passing test would prove nothing * about the `never` guard. * `RadixSelect.Trigger` itself computes `aria-controls`/`aria-expanded`/`data-state`/ * `data-placeholder` and THEN spreads whatever it receives on top (verified by reading * `@radix-ui/react-select/dist/index.mjs`) * — the same compute-then-spread ordering also present on Switch/Checkbox/Radio's triggers. This * component passes `aria-label={label}`/`aria-invalid={...}` first and `{...triggerProps}` * after, so without the `never` guard a caller's `triggerProps['aria-label']` would win over * `label` at runtime exactly the way IconButton's did before its fix. `id` and * `aria-describedby` are spread again, after `triggerProps`, from `Select`'s own top-level `id`/ * `aria-describedby` props — the ones FormField wires up — so without this guard a * `triggerProps.id` would compile, lose silently to FormField's `id` when both are given, and * win silently when FormField gives neither: reachable, and exactly the shape this component's * own guarantee rule (`design.md`) exists to close. */ export type SelectTriggerRestProps = Omit< ComponentPropsWithoutRef, 'aria-label' | 'aria-invalid' | 'aria-describedby' | 'id' | 'className' > & { 'aria-label'?: never 'aria-invalid'?: never 'aria-describedby'?: never id?: never /** `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` (this @types/react version) has no * `data-*` index signature of its own, so a plain object literal assigned to `triggerProps` * gets ordinary excess-property checking — NOT the JSX-attribute hyphenated exemption this * whole type exists to route around (that exemption is specific to a JSX opening element's * attribute list, never to a nested object literal). Without this signature, something like * `triggerProps={{ 'data-testid': 'x' }}` would fail to compile even though it's exactly the * legitimate use this prop is for. Scoped to `data-*` only — `aria-*` beyond the two banned * keys already comes through the `Omit<...>` above via Trigger's real prop type. */ [key: `data-${string}`]: unknown } /** Every standard `aria-*` attribute, each one DECLARED (not matched by a pattern) with type * `never`. That distinction is load-bearing and is not what it looks like: an index signature * over a template-literal pattern — `` { [key: `aria-${string}`]: never } `` — is **inert * against a JSX attribute**, even though it correctly rejects the same key in an ordinary * object literal. TypeScript's JSX checker looks the attribute up as a *property* of the target * type; an index signature is not a property, the lookup misses, and the hyphenated-name * exemption then waves the attribute through unchecked. (Probed against this repo's own * TypeScript 6.0, 2026-09-21: the pattern form compiled `` with zero * errors while a declared `'aria-describedby'?: never` produced TS2322 on the same line. An * optional index signature is not even syntactically legal — `?:` is rejected outright.) * Mapping over `keyof AriaAttributes` produces real declared properties for the finite set React * knows about, which is what actually enforces this. `aria-describedby` is the one exception: it * is declared on SelectProps and routed to the trigger, because FormField points it at help and * error text. */ type NoTopLevelAriaProps = { [K in Exclude]?: never } /** The top-level rest goes to `RadixSelect.Root`, which renders no DOM node — so `aria-*` keys * are declared `never` here, not merely omitted. `triggerProps` fixed the symptom for a caller * who knows that prop exists; this closes the route a caller reaches for first. * `` * still compiles and still vanishes. There is no type-level construct that closes it: the * pattern index signature is inert in JSX (above), and React declares no `data-*` properties. * Closing it for real means changing where the top-level rest lands, not the type — out of * scope here. * * `children` is excluded for a different reason: `RadixSelect.Root`'s own prop type offers it, * but this component renders its own Trigger/Portal children, so JSX children on the element * always win and a `children` prop is silently discarded. `children` is an ordinary key, so the * `Omit` does the rejecting and the declared `never` only makes the error legible — both are * shipped, matching `IconButton`. */ export type SelectProps = Omit, 'children'> & NoTopLevelAriaProps & SelectList & { 'data-testid'?: never children?: never /** Required: the trigger's accessible name. */ label?: string placeholder?: string inputSize?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' invalid?: boolean className?: string ref?: Ref /** The trigger's id, so a FormField's label and error text can point at it. */ id?: string /** Routed to the trigger, after `triggerProps`, so FormField's value wins. */ 'aria-describedby'?: string /** Extra props for the visible trigger button (e.g. `data-testid`) — NOT the same as the * top-level rest, which goes to `RadixSelect.Root`'s control props instead. See the type * comment on `SelectTriggerRestProps` for why this exists as a separate path. */ triggerProps?: SelectTriggerRestProps } const ITEM_CLASSES = cn( 'relative flex items-center gap-2 h-8 px-2 pr-8 select-none outline-none', 'font-body text-sm text-[var(--color-text-primary)]', 'data-[highlighted]:bg-[var(--color-accent-signal-indicator)]', 'data-[highlighted]:text-[var(--color-accent-signal-indicator-ink)]', disabledText, 'data-[disabled]:pointer-events-none' ) function SelectRow({ option }: { option: SelectOptionWithIcon }) { return ( {option.icon !== undefined ? ( // Outside ItemText on purpose: Radix copies ItemText into the trigger, and the trigger // shows the chosen label only. The icon inherits the row colour, so it follows the // highlight to ink with no pair of its own. {option.icon} ) : null} {option.label} ) } /** * A single choice from a list, on Radix Select. `options` is a flat list; `groups` puts the rows * under headings (Radix `Group` + `Label`, so each group is a `role="group"` named by its * heading). The heading is the mono label style in `text.secondary`, the pair DropdownMenu's own * label already gates on this surface ("dropdown menu label (text.secondary) on * surface.sunken"), and groups are split by the same `border.hairline` rule DropdownMenu's * separator paints. */ export function Select({ label, options, groups, placeholder = 'Select…', inputSize = 'md', invalid = false, className, ref, triggerProps, id, 'aria-describedby': describedBy, ...rest }: SelectProps) { return ( {groups ? groups.map((group, index) => ( {index > 0 ? ( ) : null} {group.label} {group.options.map(option => ( ))} )) : options.map(option => )} ) } // FormField passes its own label in. With the marker it does so even when none was written // here, so a Select inside a FormField needs no label of its own. Select.namedByFormField = true
